title: Load a boat of chips into a tube furnace's hot zone and seal the tube
instruction: Push the boat to the hot zone with the hook rod until its red band meets the tube's end, lay the rod back in its trough, then push the end cap fully onto the tube.
context: Loading samples into a tube furnace is a daily step in materials labs. The boat is hidden in the furnace, so the rod's band is the only cue, and a jolt slides the chips.
setup: A bench with the two arms' bases at x = 0, y = +0.30 and -0.30 m (x points away from them; heights are above the bench). A split-tube furnace, a white steel body 300 x 260 x 330 mm from x = 0.45 to 0.75 m, centred on y = 0, a red line across its lid at the hot zone's centre, x = 0.60 m. Through it runs a fused-quartz tube, 50.8 mm outside and 46 mm inside, from x = 0.33 to 0.86 m, its axis at y = 0 and 150 mm high, on two dark stands; its open end, at x = 0.33 m, faces the arms. In the tube, its back 4 mm inside that end, a fused-quartz boat 80 x 20 x 8 mm, 12 g, its back end raised into a 17 mm tab, holds three 10 x 10 x 0.5 mm silicon chips in a row, 24 mm apart. In line with the tube, a stainless hook rod lies in a dark trough on two posts (x = -0.047 to 0.082 m, an 11 mm slot): 520 mm long, 115 g, 6 mm round for its front 130 mm and 8 mm square behind, a 16 mm pusher disc and a small skid at its front, a red band 230 mm behind the pusher, the pusher at x = 0.27 m. An aluminium quick-release end cap, 100 g (a 5 mm plate, a 25 mm sleeve with a 53.4 mm bore and an O-ring, a 68 mm knurled nut next to the plate), lies in a saddle stand with its plate at x = 0.265 m, y = 0.11 m, its axis level along x and its open end towards the furnace.
scoring: 0 if a chip slides over 3 mm on the boat or tilts over 30 degrees, or the boat tilts over 20 degrees, at any time; 0 unless the boat, chips, rod and cap have moved under 1 mm over the last second, and 0 unless the boat's centre is within 10 mm of the hot zone's centre along the tube (and within 5 mm of the tube's axis). Otherwise 0.25, plus 0.25 if the rod lies in its trough within 15 mm of where it started, tilted under 5 degrees, its pusher out of the tube, plus 0.25 if the cap is home: its plate within 2 mm of the tube's end and its axis within 3 mm and 3 degrees of the tube's. 1.0 if both, and every fingertip is at least 8 cm from the rod and from the tube's end.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in Isaac Sim. The tube is drawn round; inside, the boat slides on a flat 24 mm floor between stepped walls that follow the bore. The tube's end and the cap's sleeve collide as 24-sided rings with 1.3 mm play. The O-ring is not modelled: the cap pushed fully home and square stands for a tight seal (a real cap's nut is then turned by hand). No heat, gas or vacuum; the furnace stays closed.
